subject: How to make a variable prefer a smaller when possible?

messages.author: 0631c9d875251b52
messages.subject: How to make a variable prefer a smaller when possible?
parts:
Hi Everybody,
 I have two positive_ordered random variables. While these make the model general, they lead to a problem of identifiability. I would like to artificially make them prefer smaller values when possible. How can I achieve this?

The problem I have is the following :

hf~lognormal(hf_mu,hf_sigma);
sf~lognormal(sf_mu,sf_sigma);

I would like sf>hf>0 and both sf and hf as close to zero as possible. How can I achieve this in a sensible way?
Thanks,
Sunil.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: How to make a variable prefer a smaller when possible?
parts:
On Sunday, April 19, 2015 at 8:18:33 AM UTC-4, Sunil Nandihalli wrote:
I would like sf>hf>0 and both sf and hf as close to zero as possible. How can I achieve this in a sensible way?

I don't know about sensible, but my sense is that a sequence of Pareto priors is the least bad for positive ordered vectors.  Just move the location parameter so that the prior starts at the realization of the previous element and make the shape parameter large.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to make a variable prefer a smaller when possible?
parts:
It helps to have more context in a model here. If hf and sf are
scalars, then you can declare the pair of them to be ordered and
positive as:

real<lower=0> hf;
real<lower=hf> sf;

This will guarantee sf > hf. But it can distort the posterior if
it's not physically impossible to have mean(sf) > mean(hf) but
some draw m having nsf_m < hf_m.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to make a variable prefer a smaller when possible?
parts:
Thanks Bob for the response. I will give you a little more context.

The generative process :

There are two entities:

A  and B

A private info : val_mu, val_sigma, hf, sf and sf>=hf>=0, random variable val~lognormal(val_mu,val_sigma)

B's goal is to estimate val_mu, val_sigma, hf and sf


B presents A  a value "bid" and 
A draws a "val" from "lognormal(val_mu,val_sigma)"

if(val<bid and val>hf) {
  B wins the auction and has to pay price(called second bid (sb) ) as follows :  
  if (bid>sf) {
    sb = max(val,sf)
  } else {
    sb = bid
  }
} else {
  B loses the bid.
}

The data is generated using the stan code in "second_bid_gen.stan" attached to this email. 
from the data generated from the model, I am trying to infer the values of val_mu, val_sd, hf and sf from the generated data using the stan code in "second_bid_sf.stan".

following the example in your earlier solution, I split the data into winning and losing bids. On a losing bid, one only know his own bid (referred to as lb) . But on winning a bid, we have the value we bid (referred to as wb) and the price we have to pay, second bid (referred to as sb). I realized that the following relations hold for the above generative process.

if (wb==sb) 
  sb~(pdf_of(max(val,hf))*p(sb<sf)+pdf_of(max(val,sf))*p(sb>sf)
else
  sb~pdf_of(max(val,sf))

The losing bid contributes the following term to the log-probability
log(1-cdf_of(max(hf,val))(lb) )

While I feel my above formulation is correct. I would love to hear if you find any discrepancy.

cdf_of(max(hf,val)) = cdf_hf(x)*cdf_val(x)
pdf_of(max(hf,val)) = d/dx (cdf_hf(x)*cdf_val(x)) = cdf_hf(x)*pdf_val(x) + pdf_hf(x)*cdf_val(x)

p(sb<sf) = 1-cdf_sf(sb) 
p(sf<sb) = cdf_sf(sb)

While I feel most of what I have done above is correct, I am unable to come up with a reasonable
prior distributions for sf and hf. I would greatly appreciate any help/advice you may have.

Thanks a tonne in advance.

Sunil.

 I am driving both these code using the R file "second_bid.R" (also attached to this email.)

I am unable to converge the code.
